## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

---
name: runners-are-internal-only
description: Trail runners (.entire/runners/*.json) are internal-only for now, so stale/dead runner configs left in already-scaffolded repos are acceptable UX
metadata:
  type: project
---

As of 2026-09-02, `entire runner setup` / trail runners are used only inside Entire, not by customers. So when a default runner is removed from `cmd/entire/cli/runnerdefaults/runners/`, the fact that `ensureRunnersPresent` no-ops on any repo that already has runner configs (`cmd/entire/cli/runner_init.go:27`) — leaving the dead config in place and failing entire-api's push admission forever — is accepted, not a blocker. No migration or pruning path is required.

**Why:** the population affected is a handful of internal repos whose owners can delete the file by hand; building a cleanup path would be scope for no external benefit.

**How to apply:** don't raise "existing repos keep the broken runner" as a finding on runner-default removals. Revisit if runners are ever exposed to customers, at which point the no-op-when-present behaviour becomes a real upgrade problem. Related: [[no-fluff-in-review-artifacts]].
---
name: trail-tune-command
description: "`entire runner setup` command (was `trail tune`) that scaffolds + tailors .entire/runners/*.json prompts to the repo"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d70d405d-5421-4b68-beab-2e3bcaaf25a7
---

Command is `entire runner setup [<runner>]` (renamed from `entire trail tune` on
2026-06-29; new hidden `runner` group, files cmd/entire/cli/runner_*.go). Re-running where
runners already exist offers to re-tune (interactive confirm, or --run as explicit yes).
It tailors the generic trail runner prompt templates (risk/confidence/drift/etc.) to the
actual repo. Started as a
manual exercise: the shipped templates are web-app-flavored (payments, DB migrations); for
the CLI repo the real risk surface is destructive git ops, hooks, checkpoint integrity,
transcript egress.

**Design (decided with user):**
- Model (c) hybrid: default `--print` emits a paste-ready prompt; `--run` is **headless**
  (uses the configured summary provider's `agent.TextGenerator.GenerateText`, NOT an
  interactive session) and rewrites files in place.
- v1 gathers all 4 data tiers, each best-effort/graceful-skip: repo statics (CLAUDE.md/
  AGENTS.md/README/go.mod/dirs), merged PRs+issues (shell out to `gh`), checkpoint churn
  hotspots (`strategy.ListCheckpoints` → FilesTouched counts), trail history+findings
  (`api.Client` + `fetchAllTrailReviewComments`).
- The CLI does **not** parse/load `.entire/runners/*.json` anywhere else — backend consumes
  them; `{{branch}}` etc. substituted server-side. So treat them as opaque text.
- `--run` write is **surgical**: model returns `{runner-id: new-template}`; Go swaps only
  the `prompt.template` value via original raw bytes (json.RawMessage) + `bytes.Replace`,
  `SetEscapeHTML(false)` to keep `<`/`&` literal → minimal git diff, all other fields intact.
  Overwriting OK because files are git-tracked (user reviews via `git diff`).

**Files (package cli):** trail_tune_cmd.go (command+orchestration), trail_tune_gather.go
(tiers), trail_tune_prompt.go (loading+prompt assembly), trail_tune_apply.go (parse+surgical
write), + _test.go for apply/prompt. Registered in `newTrailCmd()` in trail_cmd.go.

**Onboarding:** in a repo with no `.entire/runners/*.json`, tune offers to create
the default set first (interactive confirm, or `--yes`), then tailors them.
Defaults are EMBEDDED (`cmd/entire/cli/runnerdefaults` go:embed) — NOT
model-generated — so the structural contract (output adapter, result_type,
runtime/automation) is always valid; only templates get tailored. The embedded
templates are **minimal/high-level** (purpose line + placeholders + diff step +
output-JSON contract), not the long generic ones — kept deliberately short
because tune fills in dimensions/bands. They MUST keep the same `{{placeholder}}`
set the tuned versions use ({{branch}},{{base_branch}}, +{{previous_findings}}
for review), else `validateNewTemplate`'s no-added/no-dropped check rejects the
tailoring. Embedded defaults are a point-in-time snapshot of main's runners.

**Status:** built, lint-clean, unit tests pass, `--print` + onboarding E2E
smoke-tested. Pushed to PR #1506 (4 commits) on branch `soph/trail-tune`.
`--run` headless path not yet exercised against a real provider.

**Caution:** working tree also has pre-existing unrelated local mods to
checkpoint/open.go + strategy/manual_commit.go (source of the only `ireturn` lint findings) —
not part of this feature; separate them before committing. See [[git-stash-untracked-pitfall]].

content.text:
Not required, and nothing went wrong. That wall of text is the command's actual product in its default mode, and it's the optional half of what the command does.

`entire runner setup -y` does two separate things (`cmd/entire/cli/runner_setup.go:92`):

1. **Scaffolds `.entire/runners/*.json`** — the six default runners (`trail-risk`, `-confidence`, `-drift`, `-security`, `-review`, `-summary`). This is the part enablement needs, and it already happened before the wall printed. Check `ls .entire/runners/` — if you have six files, you're enabled. Commit them.
2. **Prints a tailoring prompt to stdout** — because you didn't pass `--run`. It gathers repo signal (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/README capped at 6k/6k/2k chars, top-level dirs, recent merged PRs and issues via `gh`, checkpoint churn hotspots, past trail findings) and embeds it plus all six current runner templates into one prompt meant to be pasted into your agent. That's tens of thousands of characters, hence the wall.

The shipped templates are generic (written for a web/backend app — payments, DB migrations), so step 2 rewords their scored dimensions for your repo. **The defaults are functional without it** — `runner_setup.go:264` explicitly reports un-tailored runners as "functional as-is". Two lines on stderr at the very bottom say the same thing, but they're easy to miss after that much scrollback.

Ways to skip the wall:

```bash
# The prompt goes to stdout; the human status lines go to stderr.
entire runner setup -y > /tmp/runner-prompt.txt

# Or do the tailoring headlessly via your configured summary provider —
# prints only "updated <file>" lines instead of the prompt.
entire runner setup -y --run
```

Re-running is safe either way: it no-ops on scaffolding once the files exist (`runner_init.go:27`) and asks before re-tuning.

One thing worth fixing on the docs side: the instructions give `-y` without saying the default mode dumps a paste-ready prompt, which is exactly why it reads as a failure. Want me to file an issue against the enablement doc, or propose wording — either `--run`, or the redirect, plus a note that the defaults work untailored?

`runRunnerSetup` calls `ensureRunnersPresent` at `cmd/entire/cli/runner_setup.go:107`, before it ever looks at `opts.run`. The `!opts.run` branch that prints the prompt is at line 138. So:

| | files created | templates rewritten |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup -y` | yes (6 defaults, if none existed) | no — prompt printed for you to paste |
| `setup -y --run` | yes (same) | yes — in place, via your summary provider |

`-y` is precisely what authorizes that write without the confirmation prompt (`runner_init.go:41` — without it and without a TTY, it refuses: *"no runner configs found under …; re-run with --yes to create the default set"*).

content.text:
Yes — exactly the six embedded defaults, byte-for-byte, with no model involvement.

They come from a `go:embed` in `cmd/entire/cli/runnerdefaults` (`runners/*.json`), and `ensureRunnersPresent` writes `f.Data` straight through (`runner_init.go:58`). Nothing is generated, merged, or repo-derived at that step. Total 6.8 KB across the six files:

| file | bytes |
| --- | --- |
| `trail-confidence.json` | 1125 |
| `trail-drift.json` | 1094 |
| `trail-review.json` | 1548 |
| `trail-risk.json` | 1077 |
| `trail-security.json` | 1119 |
| `trail-summary.json` | 881 |

Each is mostly structural config — `runtime` (agent, timeout, sandbox), `automation`, `select.trigger_types`, `output` (adapter, result type, monitor key/label/polarity) — plus a deliberately minimal prompt template. `trail-risk`'s whole template is four lines: role, `git diff origin/{{base_branch}}...HEAD`, score 0–100, output-JSON contract.

That split is the design: the embedded structural contract is always valid (so a runner can actually launch and its output parses), while the templates are short on purpose because tailoring is what fills in the repo's real dimensions and score bands. So after `setup -y` you have six working-but-generic evaluators — a risk score anchored to nothing in particular rather than to your repo's actual failure modes.

One consequence worth knowing: the templates you get must keep their `{{placeholder}}` set (`{{branch}}`, `{{base_branch}}`, plus `{{previous_findings}}` for review), because `validateNewTemplate` rejects a tailoring that adds or drops one. So if you later hand-edit them, don't remove a placeholder or `setup --run` will refuse to tune that runner.

content.text:
Your mapping is the right one, and the current flags are inverted from it. Concretely what's wrong today:

**`--run` is the flag that makes the command finish its job.** Without it, `setup` scaffolds and then stops, emitting a request for someone else to do the other half. A default mode should be the complete action, not the half one.

**`-y` doesn't answer every question the command asks.** `runner_setup.go:126` never consults `opts.assumeYes` — it only reaches `ensureRunnersPresent`. So on a repo that already has runners, `setup -y` still asks the re-tune confirm in a TTY, and on a non-TTY prints `Re-run with --run to tailor them headlessly`. `-y` means "yes to everything" everywhere else; here it means "yes to one of the two prompts". That's a defect on its own, independent of any redesign.

**`--run` also doubles as a confirmation bypass** — line 132's comment says "`--run` is taken as an explicit yes". So two flags both mean "don't ask me", with different scopes.

**And there's no `--dry-run`**; the closest thing is the default, which is why it surprises.

Mapped onto your sketch:

| | today | your model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup` (TTY) | confirm *create defaults?*, then dump prompt | one question: defaults only, or defaults + adapt? |
| `setup -y` | scaffold, dump prompt, no adaptation | scaffold + adapt |
| `setup --dry-run` | — | adapt, show the diff, write nothing |
| `setup --run` | scaffold + adapt | (gone; `-y` is this) |

One genuine decision inside "preview of adapted": it can mean *run the model and show the resulting diff without writing* (a true dry-run, costs a provider call), or *show the prompt* (cheap, but it's a preview of the request, not of the adaptation). Those are two different features and I'd keep both — `--dry-run` for the first, and today's behaviour behind an explicit `--print-prompt`, so nobody gets 40 KB unless they typed its name.

Second consideration: making `-y` adapt means it now makes a provider call and can fail on provider config, where today it's local and free. Every provider except the external-plugin path implements `GenerateText` (claudecode, codex, copilotcli, cursor, geminicli, pi), so that failure is rare — but a CI/scripted enablement path may still want scaffold-only, which argues for a `--defaults-only` escape hatch.

Worth doing now specifically because runners are still internal-only: the population that would notice a flag-semantics change is a handful of Entire repos, so it's cheap today and won't be once this is customer-facing.

Want me to implement it, or write it up as an issue first? And separately — the `-y`-doesn't-answer-the-second-prompt bug is a small standalone fix if you'd rather land that ahead of the redesign.

19	// runnerSetupMode is what one `runner setup` invocation does. The modes differ
20	// in how far they go, not in whether they ask: consent is settled once, when
21	// the mode is resolved, which is what makes --yes answer every question the
22	// command can raise. It previously answered only the create-defaults
23	// confirmation and left the tailoring one to prompt anyway.
24	type runnerSetupMode string
25	
26	const (
27		// setupModeAdapt creates the defaults when the repo has none, then tailors
28		// every runner in scope to this repo, in place. The full action, so it is
29		// what --yes and the interactive default select.
30		setupModeAdapt runnerSetupMode = "adapt"
31		// setupModeDefaults creates the generic defaults and stops. No provider call.
32		setupModeDefaults runnerSetupMode = "defaults"
33		// setupModePrintPrompt creates the defaults as needed and prints the
34		// tailoring prompt for the caller's own agent instead of running a provider.
35		setupModePrintPrompt runnerSetupMode = "print-prompt"
36		// setupModeDryRun tailors and prints the result as a diff, writing nothing —
37		// not even the defaults, so in a fresh repo it previews the embedded set.
38		setupModeDryRun runnerSetupMode = "dry-run"
39	)
40	
41	type runnerSetupOptions struct {
42		runner       string // optional: limit to one runner (id, with or without "trail-")
43		assumeYes    bool   // -y: answer every prompt, i.e. create the defaults and tailor them
44		defaultsOnly bool

53	func newRunnerSetupCmd() *cobra.Command {
54		var (
55			opts          runnerSetupOptions
56			deprecatedRun bool
57		)
58	
59		cmd := &cobra.Command{
60			Use:   "setup [<runner>]",
61			Short: "Create and tailor this repository's trail runners",
62			Long: `Set up the .entire/runners/*.json evaluators for this repository.
63	
64	Runners (risk, confidence, drift, security, review, …) score and review a
65	branch's changes. The shipped defaults are generic; setup can tailor them to
66	THIS repo using gathered signal — its docs and structure, merged PRs and
67	issues, checkpoint churn hotspots, and past trail findings.
68	
69	In a terminal with no flags, setup asks whether you want the generic defaults
70	or defaults tailored to this repo. Otherwise name the action up front:
71	
72	  -y, --yes           create the defaults if missing, then tailor them in place
73	      --defaults-only create the generic defaults and stop
74	      --print-prompt  print the tailoring prompt for your own agent to run
75	      --dry-run       show the tailoring as a diff and write nothing
76

96		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&opts.defaultsOnly, "defaults-only", false,
97			"Create the generic default runners and stop (no tailoring, no provider call)")
98		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&opts.printPrompt, "print-prompt", false,
99			"Print the tailoring prompt for your own agent instead of running a provider")
100		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&opts.dryRun, "dry-run", false,

104		cmd.Flags().IntVar(&opts.limit, "limit", 20, "How many recent PRs/issues/trails to sample")
105		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&opts.debugDir, "debug-dir", "",

41		// the raw TextGenerator rather than provider.Generator: the latter is a
42		// summarize.Generator that turns a transcript Input into a checkpoint
43		// Summary, whereas we need plain prompt->text generation here.

45		if err != nil {

51		}

78		// rather than in Go's randomized map order.

# Changelog

## [0.10.5] - 2026-09-03

### Changed

- Mirror creation goes through the control plane's async request routes by default, reporting queued, placing, and cloning progress instead of holding one request open for the whole placement; the `async_mirror_requests` setting it shipped behind in 0.10.4 now defaults on. content.text:
Implemented. `entire runner setup` now has one decision point instead of two half-answered ones.

**The new surface**

| | behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `setup` (TTY) | asks once: *create the defaults and tailor them* / *create the generic defaults only* |
| `setup -y` | creates the defaults if missing, then tailors them — the full action |
| `setup --defaults-only` | creates the generic defaults and stops; no provider call |
| `setup --print-prompt` | the old default: creates as needed, prints the prompt for your own agent |
| `setup --dry-run` | tailors and shows a diff, writes **nothing** — not even the defaults |
| `setup --run` | deprecated alias for `-y`, hidden from help, warns |

`--defaults-only`, `--print-prompt` and `--dry-run` are mutually exclusive; an explicit mode outranks `-y`, so `-y --dry-run` still writes nothing.

**What that fixed**

`resolveRunnerSetupMode` (`runner_setup.go:200`) is now the only place consent is taken, which is what makes `-y` answer everything — the two `huh` confirmations are gone, replaced by one `chooseRunnerSetupAction` select, and `ensureRunnersPresent` no longer asks at all. Non-interactive with no flag no longer half-completes: it names the four choices and exits 1 without writing.

`--dry-run` in a repo with no runners previews against the embedded set via a new `defaultTuneRunners`, so a preview of enablement leaves the repo untouched. The preview diffs each `prompt.template` rather than the JSON file — the template is the only field that changes and it's stored as one long JSON string, so a file diff would be a single unreadable line — with unchanged runs over 6 lines collapsed to `@@ N unchanged line(s) @@` so the preview doesn't become its own wall of text.

Two things I changed beyond the flags, both small: proposals are now processed in sorted order (`slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(...))`) so skip messages and the diff aren't in Go's randomized map order, and `loadTuneRunners`/`defaultTuneRunners` share one `parseTuneRunners` rather than duplicating the parse.

**Verification**

`mise run fmt` then `mise run lint` — 0 issues; `mise run test` — 10,509 tests pass. `mise run dup` shows no new duplication (the two `runner_gather.go` hits are pre-existing, in a file I didn't touch, advisory-threshold only).

13 new tests in `runner_setup_test.go`, including the behavioural pair that pins the distinction you asked about: `--dry-run` creates no `.entire/runners`, `-y` creates the full set *before* the provider is involved (so a provider failure still leaves a working generic set). Both stub `loadSummarySettings` — an existing seam `dispatch_test.go` already uses — to an unresolvable provider so no test can make a real model call. `TestClassifyTuneProposals` covers accept/reject/verbatim-no-op against canned proposals.

Also smoke-tested the real binary in throwaway repos: help text, the no-flag error, mutual exclusion, `--defaults-only` and its no-op re-run, the `--print-prompt` stdout/stderr split (prompt on stdout, status on stderr), `--run`'s deprecation warning, and that `--dry-run` leaves an existing set byte-identical.

Two things I did **not** do, since they're your call:

- **No real-provider run.** The one path still unexercised end-to-end is the actual `GenerateText` call — same as before this change. Testing it means a real model call, which CLAUDE.md says not to do proactively. Say the word and I'll run `setup --dry-run` here for real.
- **No changelog entry.** `CHANGELOG.md` has no `Unreleased` section — entries are written per release — so this belongs in the next release's pass. I can add one if you'd rather it not wait.

Nothing is committed. Want me to run the full `mise run check` and commit this on a branch, and does the enablement doc wording want updating in the same change?

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

## Findings

### 1. Seconds of gathered signal are thrown away when the provider can't resolve — and the provider prompt comes *after* the wait
- **file** `cmd/entire/cli/runner_setup.go`
- **line** 174-176 (gather) vs. `runner_apply.go:44` (provider resolution inside `runTuning`, called at `runner_setup.go:192`)

Only *then* does `runTuning` call `resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider`, which can (a) fail outright with "no summary-capable provider is available", (b) probe `$PATH` for external `entire-agent-*` plugins, or (c) **prompt the user interactively** (`promptSummaryProvider`, `explain_summary_provider.go:100`) when several providers are installed. So in the failure case the entire gather — the seconds-to-tens-of-seconds part of the command — is wasted, and in the multi-provider case the user sits through "Gathering repository signal" before being asked the question that gates it. The diff's own tests exercise exactly this path: `TestRunRunnerSetup_DryRunCreatesNothing` and `..._YesCreatesDefaultsBeforeTailoring` stub an unresolvable provider and still pay the gather.
- **cheaper** Split `runTuning` in two: resolve the provider + `agent.AsTextGenerator` before the gather spinner, pass the resolved `textGen` into the generate half. Cheap-and-fallible first, expensive-and-slow second. The diff already created the seam that makes this a small change — `runTuning`'s first 20 lines are the resolve half, with no dependency on `prompt` or `runners` beyond `len(runners)` for the spinner label.
- **honesty** This ordering is pre-existing: `applyTuneWithAgent` resolved the provider at its top too, after the same gather. The diff preserved it and extended it to a second mode (`--dry-run`). Not introduced, but this is the right patch to fix it in.

### 2. `runnerConfigsExist` runs twice (three ReadDirs of the same directory) — negligible
- **file** `cmd/entire/cli/runner_setup.go`
- **line** 134, then again inside `ensureRunnersPresent` (`runner_init.go:29`), and `loadTuneRunners` does its own `ReadDirNoSymlinks` of the same directory a third time (`runner_prompt.go:47`)
- **cost** Measured: **36.7 µs, 4.6 KB, 53 allocs** per `runnerConfigsExist` call on a populated 6-file directory. The `entiredir` root is memoized via `osroot.Shared`/`SharedChild`, so the per-call cost is just `OpenChild("runners")` (Lstat + OpenRoot + Stat + SameFile), a getdents, and a close. The duplicate costs ~37 µs against a command whose cheapest mode does a git-walk and whose main mode does an LLM round trip. Also worth knowing: for `--yes`, `--defaults-only` and `--print-prompt` the line-134 value is **dead** — `resolveRunnerSetupMode` reads `haveRunners` only on the `CanPromptInteractively()` branch, and the only other consumers are the dry-run loader swap (line 166) and `previewTunedRunners`.

### 3. `runnerdefaults.Files()` called three times, once purely to produce an integer — negligible

- **line** 86 (`chooseRunnerSetupAction`, for the count in the form title), 33 (`ensureRunnersPresent`), and `runner_prompt.go:74` (`defaultTuneRunners`)
- **cost** Measured: **2.1 µs, 7.95 KB, 21 allocs** per call. It is not free-of-copy — `embed.FS.ReadFile` returns `[]byte(ofile.f.data)`, a fresh copy — so each call duplicates the whole 6,844-byte default set. Three calls ≈ 6.4 µs and 24 KB. Line 86 copies all six files to print `%d`, and it does so on the interactive path immediately before a `huh` form that will block on human input.
- **cheaper** A `runnerdefaults.Count()` doing only `fs.ReadDir(runnersFS, "runners")` — saves the six `ReadFile` copies. Genuinely cosmetic at this size; I'd only bother because the call site reads as if `Files()` were free.

### 4. `--dry-run` builds `newRaw` for every accepted proposal and never uses it — negligible, and arguably correct
- **file** `cmd/entire/cli/runner_apply.go`
- **line** 106 (`replaceRunnerTemplate` in `classifyTuneProposals`), consumed only by `applyTunedRunners:132`; `previewTunedRunners` reads only `.runner` and `.template`
- **cost** Measured: **13.6 µs, 5.3 KB, 51 allocs** per runner (2 `json.Unmarshal`, an encode, a `bytes.Count`, a `bytes.Replace`, a `json.Valid`). At ≤6 runners that is ~82 µs and ~32 KB discarded per dry run.
- **cheaper** Nothing worth doing. `replaceRunnerTemplate` is also the check that a rewrite *is* appliable, and a preview that shows a change which would later fail to apply is worse than 82 µs. Leave it — I'm listing it only because the brief asked whether anything is computed and discarded.

### 5. diffmatchpatch: the deadline and the fold limit are both real but ~4 orders of magnitude away — no action
- **file** `cmd/entire/cli/runner_apply.go`
- **line** 202-209
- **cost/facts** `diffmatchpatch.New()` does set `DiffTimeout: time.Second` (v1.4.0 `diffmatchpatch.go:38`) and `DiffMain` derives a deadline from it, so a pathological input degrades **silently** to a crude single delete+insert rather than hanging. Measured against that: a real runner template (`trail-risk`, 395-byte template, ~12 lines) renders in **1.55 µs**. A 100%-distinct-lines worst case scales roughly quadratically — 50 lines 27 µs, 200 lines 160 µs, 500 lines 671 µs, 2000 lines **7.1 ms** — so the 1 s deadline needs on the order of 20,000 fully distinct lines, which a model-generated prompt template cannot reach (it's bounded by output tokens). On the fold limit: v1.4.0's `DiffLinesToChars` encodes line indices as runes via `intToRune` over a `uint32` `index` (`index.go`, `stringutil.go:96`), giving ~1.1M distinct lines — **not** the 65,535 of the older JS-style `DiffLinesToRunes`. No line limit to hit, no timeout to set, and `checklines=false` is the right argument since the input is already line-folded.

### 6. `gatherTuningContext` is never called for a mode that doesn't need it — correct as written
`setupModeDefaults` returns at `runner_setup.go:158` before the gather; the three modes that reach line 175 (`adapt`, `print-prompt`, `dry-run`) all consume `brief` via `buildTunePrompt`. No wasted gather by mode. (The sequential `gh`/trail I/O *inside* `gatherTuningContext` is the obvious concurrency win in this command — 2 subprocesses and ≤9 HTTP round trips that are mutually independent except for `client.SetTrailRoute`'s shared mutation — but `runner_gather.go` is not in this diff, so it's out of scope here.)

### 7. The `opts` closure: no lifetime concern, and the diff improves it
`opts` is captured by both the flag registrations (`&opts.assumeYes` …) and the `RunE` closure, so it heap-escapes and lives as long as the command tree — process lifetime. That's ~7 words plus two strings and a `[]string`, identical in kind to every other command in the tree, and the diff **reduces** the escaping variable count from five (`run`, `assumeYes`, `debugDir`, `sources`, `limit`) to one struct plus `deprecatedRun`. Nothing large is captured — no readers, buffers, `*os.Root`, or `[]tuneRunner` in the closure.

### 8. Nothing new at command-construction time
`newRunnerSetupCmd` adds only in-memory work: `MarkDeprecated` (a flag lookup + string field) and `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive` (cobra `flag_groups.go:65` — `mergePersistentFlags` on a parentless command, then 3 `Lookup` + 3 `SetAnnotation`). No I/O, no embed read, no settings load. `runnerInsecureHTTP(cmd)` correctly stayed inside `RunE`.

### 9. No O(n²), and the map building is right
`byID` (`runner_apply.go:83`) and `tailored` (`:130`) are both single-pass over ≤6 elements with capacity hints. `slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(templates))` (`:90`) adds one allocation and a sort of ≤6 keys to buy deterministic message/diff ordering — the right trade, and a strict improvement over the old randomized map iteration. `untailoredRunners` is one map lookup per created ID.

### 10. `Raw` retention, precisely: one trivial over-retention from the in-place filter
- **file** `cmd/entire/cli/runner_prompt.go`
- **line** 104 (`Raw: f.Data`) and 111 (`filtered := runners[:0]`)
- **cost** `Raw` aliases `f.Data` — no copy, so `loadTuneRunners`' new intermediate `[]runnerdefaults.File` (line 54) costs 6 extra 24-byte struct headers versus the old read-and-parse-in-one-pass loop, dropped after `parseTuneRunners` returns. Fine. The one genuine over-retention: the `--runner` filter compacts in place, so a filtered result has `len 1, cap 6` and the backing array keeps all six `tuneRunner` structs — and therefore all six `Raw` slices — reachable for the command's lifetime instead of just the selected one. **~7 KB.** Separately, each `tunedRunner` stores the new template twice (as `template` and JSON-escaped inside `newRaw`), ~50 KB for six 4 KB tailored templates; both fields are legitimately live on the apply path.
- **cheaper** `slices.DeleteFunc`, or allocate a fresh slice for the filtered result. Not worth a commit on its own.</result>

- **deeper change**: put the authority on the type and gate at the writing layer, not the call site.
  1. `func (m runnerSetupMode) writesRunnerFiles() bool` as a `switch m` with `default: return false`. This repo already has the precedent — `session.Phase` is a string enum with predicate methods (`IsActive()`) and a fail-safe normalizer (`PhaseFromString`, `session/phase.go:29`) — and `exhaustive` is enabled in `.golangci.yaml:25` with no `default-signifies-exhaustive`, so a `switch` over the mode gets *machine* enforcement that a fifth mode is handled. `runnerConfigsExist` is probed twice per invocation — once at `runner_setup.go:134` for `haveRunners`, once inside `ensureRunnersPresent` at `runner_init.go:29`. Defensible as idempotence in the writer, and it collapses for free if you take the `prepareRunners` variant of finding 2.</result>

content.text:
Clean: 0 lint issues, 0 duplication hits in the touched files, 10,509 unit tests pass.

## Fixed

**Reuse** — `runTuning` was re-deriving a `TextGenerator` via `agent.Get` + `agent.AsTextGenerator`, but `resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider` already returns one on `provider.TextGenerator`, guaranteed non-nil by its constructor. Dropped 8 lines, two unreachable error branches, and the whole `agent` import from `runner_apply.go`. Tests now reuse the existing `writeRunner`/`mustJSONString` helpers instead of a second hand-rolled JSON builder that silently dropped escaping, and `newRunnerSetupRepo` pairs `t.Chdir` with `paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache` like every comparable fixture.

**Efficiency** — the provider is now resolved *before* `gatherTuningContext`, not after. Resolution can fail outright or stop to ask which provider to use, and both were happening after two `gh` subprocesses, a git walk, and up to nine trail API round trips. Verified: the failure now lands with no "Gathering repository signal" spinner at all. Also killed the duplicate `runnerConfigsExist` probe and made the `--runner` filter allocate a fresh slice — compacting in place kept every unselected runner's file bytes reachable through the shared array.

**Altitude** — `runnerSetupMode`'s zero value used to authorize the *most* invasive path: `mode == ""` passed `!= setupModeDryRun`, scaffolded, and fell through to `applyTunedRunners`. Consent is now a fail-closed predicate, `mode.writesRunnerFiles()`, with a total switch — which `exhaustive` enforces, and which promptly caught my tail switch as incomplete. `createDefaultRunners` (renamed from `ensureRunnersPresent`) no longer re-derives existence; the caller's guard is the single home for that invariant, so the doc comment's "callers must not reach here without consent" is now code. The loader swap is expressed as the rule (`!mode.writesRunnerFiles() && !haveRunners`) rather than the instance, and `previewTunedRunners` lost its `haveRunners` parameter — the provenance notice now prints at the swap site, where the fact is actually known, so it can't drift out of step.

**Simplification** — one `reportCreatedDefaults` replaces three copies of the same sentence whose wording had already drifted ("default" / "generic default" / "working default"). `--sources`/`--limit` are validated after the mode, so `--defaults-only --limit 0` no longer fails for flags it never reads (verified). The picker now routes cancellation through the shared `handleFormCancellation`, so Ctrl+C prints "Runner setup cancelled." and exits 0 like the other 17 pickers. The non-interactive error names the four flags without re-teaching `--help`. Tests got a `runnerFiles` helper and derive the default-set size from the embed instead of hardcoding `6` in four places.

One stub was genuinely wrong and worth calling out: I had `stubUnavailableSummaryProvider` assert discovery never runs, but production legitimately calls it when the agent lookup fails — so it's now a silent no-op, which is what actually keeps the test off the developer's real `$PATH`. That $PATH dependency was real: the old stub only replaced `loadSummarySettings`, leaving `external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` to glob and exec `entire-agent-*` binaries.

## Skipped

- **`runnerdefaults.File` as an on-disk carrier** — the two agents split on this, and the suggested fix (a local identical `{Name, Data}` type) adds a mapping loop to avoid coupling that's theoretical. The type is a generic pair.
- **`runnerdefaults.Count()`** — 2µs, and a new public API on the embed package to render one form title isn't worth it.
- **Collapsing the three mode booleans into one `mode` field** — the agent itself called it line-neutral. Cobra's `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive` already prevents the impossible combinations, and `-y` + a mode flag is a *reachable* conflict that stays tested. Keeping the change reviewable won.
- **Removing `tuneRunner.Path`** — pre-existing field, used in error messages; churn beyond this diff.
- **Splitting into `runner init` + `runner tune`** — the altitude agent argued this is the deeper fix and made a decent case (the file layout already found that seam, `--defaults-only` inherits four flags it can't use, and the picker only ever offers 2 of the 4 modes). It explicitly didn't recommend it since you asked for the four-mode shape. Flagging it as a real note rather than acting on it — worth knowing if runners ever go customer-facing.
- **Making `gatherTuningContext`'s `gh`/trail I/O concurrent** — the obvious remaining win in this command (2 subprocesses and ≤9 independent HTTP round trips, all sequential), but `runner_gather.go` isn't in this diff.

Still uncommitted, and the actual `GenerateText` call is still the one path never exercised end-to-end.
